speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the nature of your cough, and do you have any fever or chest pain? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count, Chest X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count: WBC 9,000 /μL, Hemoglobin 14.0 g/dL, Platelets 230,000 /μL; Chest X-Ray: Bilateral interstitial infiltrates suggestive of pulmonary fibrosis. No pleural effusion or pneumothorax observed.

speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any worsening of your breathlessness with exertion? REQUEST TEST: Pulmonary Function Tests (PFTs).

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pulmonary Function Tests: Reduced FVC and FEV1 with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio, indicating a restrictive pattern.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you ever been exposed to asbestos, bird droppings, or other industrial dusts, and do you have a history of autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis or scleroderma? REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune Panel (ANA, RF, CCP).

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; since your autoimmune panel is normal, we can likely rule out connective tissue diseases. Have you noticed any dry eyes or dry mouth, and do you have a history of kidney stones or gallstones? REQUEST TEST: Schirmer's Test, Anti-Ro/La Antibodies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the normal Schirmer's test and negative Anti-Ro/La antibodies make Sjögren's syndrome unlikely. Given the restrictive lung pattern and interstitial infiltrates, have you noticed any clubbing of your fingers or toes, and do you have a history of skin rashes or joint pain? REQUEST TEST: High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the chest.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: High-Resolution CT (HRCT) of the chest: Ground-glass opacities and reticular markings consistent with interstitial lung disease. No evidence of honeycombing or significant emphysema.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you ever smoked, and do you have any history of occupational exposure to silica, coal dust, or metal fumes? REQUEST TEST: Serum Soluble Receptor for Advanced Glycation End-products (sRAGE) and Alpha-1 Antitrypsin levels.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you experienced any recent weight loss, night sweats, or fatigue, and do you have a history of tuberculosis or other chronic infections? REQUEST TEST: Quantiferon Gold Test.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the results; the negative Quantiferon Gold test makes an active tuberculosis infection unlikely. Given the restrictive pattern, ground-glass opacities, and negative autoimmune workup, have you noticed any improvement or worsening of your symptoms after taking specific medications, and do you have any family history of lung disease? REQUEST TEST: Serum KL-6 and Surfactant Protein D levels.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Serum KL-6: Elevated; Surfactant Protein D: Elevated

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the elevated KL-6 and SP-D levels alongside your restrictive lung disease and negative autoimmune workup, have you noticed any skin changes like telangiectasias or calcinosis, and do you have a history of Raynaud's phenomenon? REQUEST TEST: Nailfold Capillaroscopy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Nailfold Capillaroscopy: Dilated and tortuous capillaries with loss of the normal three-tier structure, consistent with scleroderma spectrum disorder.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Limited Cutaneous Systemic Sclerosis (CREST Syndrome) with Interstitial Lung Disease.
